top.title: Bellingham beauty in Real Madrid win; Arsenal, Man City held in Champions League
top.description: Jude Bellingham scored one of the goals of the season as Real Madrid hammered PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday to maintain their perfect record in this season’s Champions League, while Arsenal and Manchester City were both held to draws at home. Elsewhere, debutants Como and Real Betis continued their excellent form since the start of the league phase, but Aston Villa slumped to another defeat on their travels. Record 15-time European champions Real had to come from behind to beat PSV at the Bernabeu as they made it five wins from five in this season’s league phase to go clear at the top of the standings with 15 points. Dutch champions PSV led at half-time courtesy of an Ivan Perisic penalty, but Federico Valverde equalised five minutes after the restart. Bellingham then put Real ahead on the hour with a remarkable strike, as he controlled a Kylian Mbappe lay-off outside the box and then teed himself up for a sweet volley on the outside of his right boot which flew into the corner of the net. Mbappe then scored twice to move to 19 goals in all competitions this season and 76 career Champions League goals. The France captain now has 105 Real Madrid goals, one more than the Brazilian Ronaldo managed for the club. Vinicius Junior sealed the win for Jose Mourinho’s side, who have now claimed 10 consecutive victories in all competitions. “That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and then I just hit it. I thought I would go with the outside of the boot a little bit, stab it a little bit, I am not one for smashing the ball too hard. It was a nice moment,” England star Bellingham told British broadcaster TNT Sports about his goal. Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain can join Real at the top of the standings if they beat Roma on Wednesday, but Como and Betis are currently level with the French side on 12 points after they beat AEK Athens and Slovan Bratislava respectively. Como and Betis flying Luis Milla scored as Como beat AEK 1-0 in Italy after Lucas Da Cunha earlier squandered a penalty, while Cucho Hernandez grabbed both goals for Betis in their 2-0 victory in Slovakia. Arsenal had to settle for a point after drawing 1-1 with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium, as Viktor Gyokeres put the Gunners ahead but later missed a golden chance to win the game. Gyokeres opened the scoring with a thunderous strike, but Maximilian Beier equalised for Dortmund and the Arsenal striker headed woefully wide from Martin Odegaard’s cross late on. It is the second time Arsenal, last season’s beaten finalists, have dropped points to German opposition this season following a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich. Manchester City are in the midst of a poor run of form in the Premier League and Enzo Maresca’s side had to come from behind twice in the second half to draw 2-2 against Napoli. top.title: No. 3 Florida Basketball Survives to Avoid Huge Upset
top.description: Photo by: Alan Youngblood The No. 3 Florida Gators narrowly avoided one of the biggest upsets of the college basketball season Tuesday night, defeating Milwaukee 76-67 at Tower Hill Arena in Gainesville. Florida entered the matchup as a massive favorite, expected to handle a Milwaukee team that had struggled through the early portion of its season. Instead, the Gators found themselves in a much closer contest than anticipated, needing a strong second-half performance to secure the nine-point victory. The win improves Florida’s record to 7-1, but the performance raises questions about a team that entered the season with national championship expectations. Milwaukee Gives Florida a Scare Milwaukee deserves credit for making this a competitive game. The Panthers played with confidence and refused to back down against one of the nation’s top teams. Florida was favored by more than 30 points, but Milwaukee managed to keep the game within reach throughout the first half. The Panthers trailed just 37-34 at halftime, putting pressure on the Gators to find another gear after the break. The game remained competitive deep into the second half, with Milwaukee cutting Florida’s lead to just two points at one stage. For a team expected to cruise to an easy victory, the Gators suddenly found themselves in danger of suffering an embarrassing home loss. Milwaukee’s Chandler Jackson led the Panthers with 20 points, while Al Amadou contributed 13. The Panthers also knocked down 10 three pointers, making it difficult for Florida to create separation. Rueben Chinyelu Comes Up Huge The biggest reason Florida escaped with the victory was the outstanding performance from Rueben Chinyelu. Chinyelu delivered a career high 25 points and grabbed 16 rebounds, recording his first double-double of the season. He was extremely efficient, shooting 10-of-12 from the field and making all four of his free throws. When Florida needed someone to take control, Chinyelu answered. His presence around the basket helped the Gators establish an advantage inside, and his offensive rebounding gave Florida important second-chance opportunities. Thomas Haugh also delivered a strong performance, finishing with 16 points and eight rebounds. Denzel Aberdeen added 14 points, providing another important scoring option. Florida ultimately controlled the paint, outscoring Milwaukee 40-22 in that area while winning the rebounding battle 45-24. Gators Have Plenty to Clean Up Although Florida avoided the upset, Tuesday’s performance showed that the team still has plenty of work to do. The Gators cannot afford to overlook opponents, especially with a challenging schedule ahead. Their defensive intensity was inconsistent, allowing Milwaukee to remain within striking distance for much of the night. Head coach Todd Golden will likely use this performance as a teaching opportunity. top.title: Scoring Milestone | FC’s Hadli Gillum scores her 1,000th career point
top.description: LANCASTER - On a night when Fisher Catholic junior Hadli Gillum had a chance to reach a major scoring milestone, it wasn't a matter of if, but a matter of when she would do it. Needing 23 points to reach 1,000 career points, Gillum missed her first two shots, including an uncontested layup. Maybe it was nerves, maybe it was all the people in the stands, holding up signs and counting down, but for Gillum, she is a scorer, and it didn’t take her long to get going after those first two misses. Gillum scored 17 points in the first quarter against Cristo Rey, and after scoring two more baskets to get to 21 points, Gillum was to reach the 1,000-point plateau when she received the ball in the post, to a couple dribbles to her left, then quickly came back to the right and laid it in off the glass. Her teammates congratulated her, and the game stopped to recognize her accomplishment. More: Fisher Catholic's Hadli Gillum is a sophomore basketball sensation “This has definitely been a goal I’ve had my whole life, ever since I started watching my older sister play and past players like Voni Bethel. Watching them get it, it was a goal of mine coming into high school,” Gillum said. “I didn’t expect it to be this early, but I am very excited and grateful for the opportunity and the community and the support we have here. It was loud in here, and the love and support meant a lot to me. "It has been stressful only because everyone was talking about it, and my friends were asking what if I didn’t get it. I knew it was going to come eventually, so I wasn’t worried about it that much, although I did miss that easy layup early in the game, and all I could do was laugh.” Gillum, who only played in the first half as the Irish cruised to a 57-8 victory, scored 25 points on 12 of 18 shooting. She added four assists, three rebounds and four steals. Gillum has now scored 1,002 career points in 53 games played. Who knows where her career total will end up with basically two full seasons remaining. Gillum, who was the 2025 Eagle-Gazette Girls Basketball Player of the Year and earned first-team All-Ohio honors in both her freshman and sophomore seasons, has shown she can score in a variety of different ways. She is an outstanding passer, making sure she always gets her teammates involved. A year ago, she helped lead the Irish to a 22-4 record, an undefeated Mid-State League-Cardinal Division championship and a second straight Central District Division VII district title. Gillum averaged 22.1 points, 6.5 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 1.8 steals per game. top.title: Georgia ranked No. 1 in fourth College Football Playoff rankings
top.description: The fourth edition of the 2026-27 College Football Playoff rankings was released on Nov. 24, and the Georgia Bulldogs stayed put as the top spot in the rankings for the third straight week in a row. They probably added some distance after blowing out South Carolina 34-6. They've beaten four straight ranked SEC opponents by double digits. They beat No. 17 (AP) Florida, No. 10 Ole Miss , No. 22 Missouri, and No. 21 South Carolina. With the win, they clinched a spot in the SEC championship, their sixth appearance in a row in the SEC championship. Considering the status of the SEC and the rest of the College Football Playoff, the Bulldogs are almost certain to make the CFP. Speaking of the SEC, the biggest surprises came with the way they dealt with the other three that are in the CFP: Texas, Tennessee, and Alabama. They rose Texas to the No. 3 spot, increased Tennessee to No. 5, and brought down Alabama to No. 6. The Big Ten also experienced a ton of changes. UCLA is the only team in the conference that's still in the CFP. They lost 18-16 in 3OT to Michigan, bringing them down from No. 4 to No. 9. Indiana, meanwhile, fell all the way down from No. 8 to No. 14 after their 27-24 overtime loss to Washington. The Oregon Ducks passed them up, becoming the No. 12 team and the first one out of the CFP. The Indiana fall brought in a new addition to the CFP: 10-1 Texas Tech. Once again, just like the last two weeks, Georgia would get a first-round bye if this holds. They would play the winner of the game between Wake Forest and UCLA. Both of those teams have a 10-1 record, but with very different resumes. Wake Forest has won by 21 or more points in their past seven games, while UCLA hasn't won by more than 20 against a Big Ten opponent since the Maryland game. It'll be a big test for either squad against Georgia. top.title: CFP chair Hunter Yurachek explains UCLA's No. 9 ranking
top.description: UCLA Bruins RB Wayne Knight (3) celebrates after scoring a rushing touchdown during a game against San Diego State Aztecs at Rose Bowl Stadium on September 12, 2026 in Pasadena, California. UCLA football dropped from No. 4 to No. 9 in the Nov. 24 edition of the College Football Playoff (CFP) rankings, marking one of the more notable shifts in this week’s top 25. The drop came after the Bruins’ first loss of the season, an 18-16 triple overtime contest at Michigan which put them at 10-1. Despite the loss, they remain the highest-ranked team in the Big Ten and the only Big Ten team currently in the playoff bracket, followed by No. 12 Oregon, who is currently the first team out. Other Big Ten teams still seemingly in contention include No. 13 Iowa and No. 14 Indiana, although the committee appears to believe UCLA currently has a somewhat sizable advantage over them. “UCLA right now is not evaluated with those other three teams,” CFP chair Hunter Yurachek told ESPN’s Rece Davis. “They do have the head-to-head over Oregon.” In a selection committee media teleconference following the release of the rankings, Yurachek noted that during this week’s discussions, the committee most directly compared UCLA to three teams not in their conference: No. 8 Wake Forest, No. 10 BYU and No. 11 Texas Tech. “Wake Forest is a hot team,” Yurachek said. “They’ve won eight consecutive games, and most of those games have not even been close. And so they’ve got a lot of respect for the committee. “UCLA also has a great deal of respect from the committee. We had them at four last week. They lost a triple overtime game on the road at Michigan, a team that was 5-5. They’ve got a win over a team that we currently have ranked 12th in Oregon, and then when you start comparing them to BYU, BYU’s a two-loss team. BYU’s got really good wins, one over Notre Dame and another over Arizona. They’ve got two losses, one to No. 2 Utah and then another to Central Florida, and so we start mixing and matching these teams, you look at strength of schedule, key wins, losses. That’s how that shook out with Wake Forest, UCLA, BYU, and Texas Tech.” Yurachek was adamant in multiple comments that the uncertain status of Bruins quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who was injured late in the game against Michigan, did not play a factor in where UCLA was ranked. “UCLA fell from four to nine because they lost the game in triple overtime to Michigan,” Yuracheck told Davis. “It did not have anything to do with the injury to the quarterback that happened in the overtime period.” “They played a game [for] four-plus quarters with him at quarterback,” he continued in the teleconference. “They had an overtime period that they did not have him. We’ll continue to evaluate UCLA in their game versus USC this weekend.”

This year, like pretty much every year since it came into being, the CFP committee has been blasted for offering contradictory rankings that seemingly change on a whim on a weekly basis. And has been proven for years , the weekly ranking shows that air every Tuesday on ESPN are then thrown out the window and proven to be completely meaningless when the committee puts together the only rankings that actually matter at the end of the season. But that hasn’t stopped ESPN and the College Football Playoff committee for continuing the charade and raising the blood pressure of college football fans and media every week by continuing the drama. This year has been no exception, with the chief complaint being Alabama’s lofty ranking compared to, well, everyone else that watches college football. top.title: Vikings’ Kevin O’Connell Gets Blunt on Bijan Robinson Before Falcons Game
top.description: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty The Minnesota Vikings are looking for a bounce-back win after their Week 11 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Nonetheless, they’ll have a challenging task at home when they face the Atlanta Falcons, who are 3-7. Despite the Falcons’ record, they’ll be leaning on their weapons, one of them being running back Bijan Robinson. The Falcons star has played 460 total snaps this season, leading to an 84.6 overall PFF grade . Moreover, he carried the ball 185 times for 951 rushing yards and six touchdowns while averaging 5.1 yards per attempt on the ground and forcing 37 missed tackles as a runner. Meanwhile, as a receiver, he caught 35 passes on 42 targets for 256 receiving yards and one touchdown. As a result, Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell knows that they will need to contain Robinson if they want to secure a win. “I expect he’s going to get a high volume of carries,” O’Connell said on the Nov. 24 edition of “X’s and O’s with Kevin O’Connell.” “I expect they’ll try to come in here and run the football. We have to have a great day shutting down the run. We have to have a great day tackling, making sure there are no loose-yardage plays. “When Bijan breaks a tackle, it’s not like he’s just going to gain another three or four yards. He can take it the distance at any time [and] he can catch it. He’s a part of their passing game and lethal in the screen game. nigeria.description: Jude Bellingham scored one of the goals of the season as Real Madrid hammered PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday to maintain their perfect record in this season’s Champions League, while Arsenal and Manchester City were both held to draws at home. nigeria.title: Trump, NATO chief to meet amid Ukraine security concerns
nigeria.description: United States President Donald Trump is scheduled to meet NATO Secretary-General, Mark Rutte, today, amid growing concerns over European security and the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine. The meeting, expected to take place in Palm Beach, Florida, comes as Washington and its European allies continue discussions over the future of Ukraine, military support and security guarantees for the war-torn country. According to Reuters, the White House announced the planned meeting, while NATO also confirmed Rutte’s visit to the United States. The discussions are expected to focus on transatlantic security relations, NATO’s defence commitments and efforts to find a diplomatic solution to the conflict between Moscow and Kyiv. Trump has repeatedly called on European members of NATO to increase their defence spending and take greater responsibility for the security of the continent. The meeting also comes amid disagreements among Western allies over the terms of a possible peace agreement and the extent of future military assistance to Ukraine. Rutte has maintained that NATO’s support for Ukraine remains important to European security, as Russia’s invasion continues to shape diplomatic and military calculations across the region. The outcome of Wednesday’s meeting could provide further indications of Washington’s position on NATO’s future role in the Ukraine conflict. nigeria.title: Police declare 9 wanted over parcel of bullets sent to First Bank MD
nigeria.description: The police have declared nine persons wanted over an alleged threat to the life of First Bank of Nigeria Ltd. Managing Director, Mr. Olusegun Alebiosu. The Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG), Zone 2, Mr Olohundare Jimoh, disclosed this on Tuesday in Lagos. Jimoh spoke while briefing journalists at the Zone 2 Police Command headquarters, Onikan. He said the threat involved a parcel containing two rounds of 7.62mm live ammunition delivered to Alebiosu’s residence. The parcel, packaged as a fashion-design gift, was delivered by a dispatch rider whose identity remained unknown. He said the incident was reported to the police on May 7, while the parcel was opened the following morning. Jimoh described the ammunition as dangerous, noting that the 7.62mm rounds were designed for compatible firearms, including AK-47 rifles. He said the discovery prompted a discreet investigation to identify those behind the alleged threat. A joint team of crime detectives, ballistic experts and forensic investigators was subsequently constituted to investigate the incident. According to him, preliminary investigations revealed that First Bank had undertaken extensive loan recovery activities involving customers allegedly owing several billions of naira. Some of the customers reportedly confronted bank representatives and issued threats against the managing director during the recovery process. Jimoh said the investigation was intended to establish the facts and identify those responsible for the alleged threat. He disclosed that 10 bank customers and other persons considered relevant to the investigation had been invited for questioning. The AIG said the invitations were issued in accordance with established investigative procedures and relevant legal provisions. He said the investigation complied with the Judges’ Rules, the 1999 Constitution, the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015, and other applicable laws. Jimoh said the Firearms Act prohibited unlawful possession or control of ammunition without appropriate legal authorisation. He disclosed that the 10 persons were invited on Nov. 5 to appear for questioning on Nov. 12. However, only one person honoured the invitation, while the remaining nine failed to report. Consequently, the police declared the nine persons wanted to facilitate the investigation into the alleged threat against Alebiosu and his family. Jimoh urged anyone with useful information about their whereabouts to report to the nearest police station. He assured the public that the investigation would remain discreet and professional, adding that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law. The AIG stressed that nobody was above the law and that the police would ensure justice was served. He added that the rights of both the suspects and the complainant would be protected throughout the investigation. nigeria.description: The Zamfara State Government yesterday inaugurated a committee to review and address the non-implementation of revised salary structures and other staff welfare issues in the state-owned tertiary institutions. The Secretary to the State Government and Chairman of the Committee, Malam Abubakar Mohammad Nakwada, inaugurated the committee and chaired its maiden meeting in Gusau, the state capital. He further emphasised that Governor Dauda Lawal has proven to be workers-friendly, citing the upward review of the minimum wage from paltry N7,000 to N70,000, the clearing of the backlog of gratuities, the implementation of a new salary scale for healthcare workers, and other welfare commitments of the current administration. “This assignment is a clear demonstration of Governor Lawal’s commitment to the welfare of workers, industrial harmony, and the development of our tertiary institutions. “The demands presented by the Forum of Zamfara State Tertiary Institutions (FOZASTI) and the Zamfara State University on salary, allowances and promotion benefits have been a source of concern. We must listen to all parties, examine the facts and figures dispassionately, and come up with recommendations that are implementable, affordable and just. “I assure the staff unions and management of our institutions that this Government is not unmindful of their plight. nigeria.title: 2027: KDI records 124 attacks, 22 deaths ahead of polls
nigeria.description: 53 days to elections, group warns of escalating political violence By John Alechenu, Abuja ABUJA — The Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI) has raised the alarm over escalating political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, disclosing that its monitoring has recorded 124 incidents and 22 deaths across 35 states and the Federal Capital Territory between July 1 and November 23, 2026. The organisation warned that the growing incidents of violence and intimidation could undermine the credibility of the elections if urgent measures were not taken to address the situation. KDI released the figures on Tuesday under its Nigeria Election Violence Education and Reporting (NEVER) Project, 53 days before the January 16, 2027 presidential and National Assembly elections. According to the organisation, incidents of electoral violence increased sharply following the commencement of political campaigns, rising from three cases in July to 48 in October, while 40 incidents were recorded in the first half of November alone. “The overall trajectory suggests that electoral competition is becoming increasingly accompanied by violence and intimidation. If left unchecked, these trends could intensify further as election day approaches,” KDI said. The organisation noted that political violence was no longer restricted to traditionally identified hotspots, with Kano, Delta, Rivers, Edo, Ondo and Kebbi recording significant incidents, while several other parts of the country were also affected. Breaking down the incidents, KDI said physical assaults accounted for 46.8 per cent of reported cases, property destruction 28.8 per cent, shootings 10.2 per cent, intimidation and harassment nine per cent, and kidnappings four per cent. It also expressed concern over the growing use of hostile rhetoric, threats and inflammatory statements across political party lines, warning that such language could normalise violence and embolden supporters. The organisation identified political party members and affiliated groups as perpetrators in 82.3 per cent of the recorded incidents, while members of political parties were victims in 86.5 per cent of the cases. “Political leaders must take concrete measures to discourage violence, sanction supporters who engage in unlawful conduct, and publicly demonstrate their commitment to peaceful elections,” it said. KDI also raised concerns over growing political intolerance, including restrictions on opposition activities, alleged abuse of administrative authority and denial of equal opportunities to campaign. On accountability, the organisation said that despite several arrests reported since January, it had found no publicly available evidence of corresponding prosecutions or convictions in many of the cases. “This accountability deficit weakens deterrence and can create the perception that perpetrators of electoral violence can act with impunity,” it warned. nigeria.title: Zamfara gov’t suspends campaign after road crash
nigeria.description: The Zamfara government has suspended its scheduled campaign activities in Maru Local Government Area following a road accident that killed 15 APC supporters. The victims died along the Gummi-Daki-Takwas-Anka route while travelling to Talata Mafara for the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally. The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) confirmed that 15 people died, while 27 others sustained injuries in the crash. The accident occurred at about 12.30 p.m. on Monday near Kisami village, along the Gummi-Daki-Takwas-Anka route. The government announced the suspension in a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Mahmud Dantawasa, on Monday in Gusau. Dantawasa said the accident involved APC members travelling from Gummi Local Government Area. “The government expresses its deep sorrow over the unfortunate incident and extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families,” he said. He also extended condolences to the Gummi Emirate and the APC family in Zamfara over the loss. The commissioner said the government sympathised with the injured and prayed for their speedy recovery. “In this moment of grief, the Zamfara State Government stands in solidarity with the affected families and all those mourning the loss of their loved ones,” he said. He urged residents to remain calm and offer prayers for the deceased and injured. “May Almighty Allah forgive the souls of the departed, grant them Aljannatul Firdaus, and give their families the strength and patience to bear this irreparable loss,” Dantawasa said. nigeria.title: Nigeria Is Cutting The Budget, But Not The Deficit
nigeria.description: The economic signal this week is that the Federal Government has acknowledged that its 2026 budget is larger than it can credibly implement. President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing total expenditure from ₦68.323 trillion to ₦65.176 trillion, a cut of approximately ₦3.15 trillion, or 4.6 per cent. Budget revision is not inherently a sign of failure. Governments should adjust spending plans when revenue, financing conditions or obligations change. An unrealistic budget does not become credible merely because it has been signed into law. The more important signal is what remains unchanged: a ₦31.457 trillion fiscal deficit and planned new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion. Nigeria is reducing expenditure, but it is not reducing the gap between what government earns and what it intends to spend. What Is Being Revised Under the proposed framework, projected federal revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at ₦33.720 trillion. Capital expenditure is estimated at ₦26.232 trillion, while the deficit remains equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP. The borrowing plan comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic financing and ₦10.790 trillion from external sources. The government says its proposed $7.7 billion foreign loan will fund an existing external-borrowing provision rather than increase the approved envelope. President Bola Tinubu signed into law the Appropriation (Amendment) (No.4) Bill, 2025, on September 30, 2026. The administration says the revision will regularise expenditure incurred by NNPC Limited on behalf of the Federation, address debt-service obligations that were underprovided for, recognise already issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and refund ministries and special accounts. Some new allocations are also proposed for critical roads, agriculture, farm productivity, market access and water security. These may be legitimate obligations. But their late recognition exposes weaknesses in the original budget’s preparation. The Credibility Problem The 2026 budget began as an executive proposal of approximately ₦58.47 trillion. It was subsequently expanded and signed at ₦68.323 trillion in April. Seven months later, the executive is asking Parliament to reduce it. The new figure remains ₦6.7 trillion above the original proposal. This sequence matters because Nigeria’s budget has become less a binding financial plan than a collection of ambitions, negotiated additions and subsequent corrections. Ministries receive large appropriations but often wait months for releases. Projects are announced without complete financing. Unpaid obligations accumulate and eventually return as supplementary provisions. A smaller, executable budget would be preferable to a larger one that exists chiefly on paper. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. sports.description: Photo by: Alan Youngblood The No. 3 Florida Gators narrowly avoided one of the biggest upsets of the college basketball season Tuesday night, defeating Milwaukee 76-67 at Tower Hill Arena in Gainesville. Florida entered the matchup as a massive favorite, expected to handle a Milwaukee team that had struggled through the early portion of its season. Instead, the Gators found themselves in a much closer contest than anticipated, needing a strong second-half performance to secure the nine-point victory. The win improves Florida’s record to 7-1, but the performance raises questions about a team that entered the season with national championship expectations. Milwaukee Gives Florida a Scare Milwaukee deserves credit for making this a competitive game. The Panthers played with confidence and refused to back down against one of the nation’s top teams. Florida was favored by more than 30 points, but Milwaukee managed to keep the game within reach throughout the first half. The Panthers trailed just 37-34 at halftime, putting pressure on the Gators to find another gear after the break. The game remained competitive deep into the second half, with Milwaukee cutting Florida’s lead to just two points at one stage. For a team expected to cruise to an easy victory, the Gators suddenly found themselves in danger of suffering an embarrassing home loss. Milwaukee’s Chandler Jackson led the Panthers with 20 points, while Al Amadou contributed 13. The Panthers also knocked down 10 three pointers, making it difficult for Florida to create separation. Rueben Chinyelu Comes Up Huge The biggest reason Florida escaped with the victory was the outstanding performance from Rueben Chinyelu. Chinyelu delivered a career high 25 points and grabbed 16 rebounds, recording his first double-double of the season. He was extremely efficient, shooting 10-of-12 from the field and making all four of his free throws. When Florida needed someone to take control, Chinyelu answered. His presence around the basket helped the Gators establish an advantage inside, and his offensive rebounding gave Florida important second-chance opportunities. Thomas Haugh also delivered a strong performance, finishing with 16 points and eight rebounds. Denzel Aberdeen added 14 points, providing another important scoring option. Florida ultimately controlled the paint, outscoring Milwaukee 40-22 in that area while winning the rebounding battle 45-24. Her teammates congratulated her, and the game stopped to recognize her accomplishment. I knew it was going to come eventually, so I wasn’t worried about it that much, although I did miss that easy layup early in the game, and all I could do was laugh.” Gillum, who only played in the first half as the Irish cruised to a 57-8 victory, scored 25 points on 12 of 18 shooting. sports.title: CFP chair Hunter Yurachek explains UCLA's No. 9 ranking
sports.description: UCLA Bruins RB Wayne Knight (3) celebrates after scoring a rushing touchdown during a game against San Diego State Aztecs at Rose Bowl Stadium on September 12, 2026 in Pasadena, California. UCLA football dropped from No. 4 to No. 9 in the Nov. 24 edition of the College Football Playoff (CFP) rankings, marking one of the more notable shifts in this week’s top 25. The drop came after the Bruins’ first loss of the season, an 18-16 triple overtime contest at Michigan which put them at 10-1. Despite the loss, they remain the highest-ranked team in the Big Ten and the only Big Ten team currently in the playoff bracket, followed by No. 12 Oregon, who is currently the first team out. Other Big Ten teams still seemingly in contention include No. 13 Iowa and No. 14 Indiana, although the committee appears to believe UCLA currently has a somewhat sizable advantage over them. “UCLA right now is not evaluated with those other three teams,” CFP chair Hunter Yurachek told ESPN’s Rece Davis. “They do have the head-to-head over Oregon.” In a selection committee media teleconference following the release of the rankings, Yurachek noted that during this week’s discussions, the committee most directly compared UCLA to three teams not in their conference: No. 8 Wake Forest, No. 10 BYU and No. 11 Texas Tech. “Wake Forest is a hot team,” Yurachek said. “They’ve won eight consecutive games, and most of those games have not even been close. And so they’ve got a lot of respect for the committee. “UCLA also has a great deal of respect from the committee. We had them at four last week. They lost a triple overtime game on the road at Michigan, a team that was 5-5. They’ve got a win over a team that we currently have ranked 12th in Oregon, and then when you start comparing them to BYU, BYU’s a two-loss team. BYU’s got really good wins, one over Notre Dame and another over Arizona. They’ve got two losses, one to No. 2 Utah and then another to Central Florida, and so we start mixing and matching these teams, you look at strength of schedule, key wins, losses. That’s how that shook out with Wake Forest, UCLA, BYU, and Texas Tech.” Yurachek was adamant in multiple comments that the uncertain status of Bruins quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who was injured late in the game against Michigan, did not play a factor in where UCLA was ranked. “UCLA fell from four to nine because they lost the game in triple overtime to Michigan,” Yuracheck told Davis. “It did not have anything to do with the injury to the quarterback that happened in the overtime period.” “They played a game [for] four-plus quarters with him at quarterback,” he continued in the teleconference. “They had an overtime period that they did not have him. We’ll continue to evaluate UCLA in their game versus USC this weekend.”

technology.title: Dell and HPE both say they’ve become ‘different companies’
technology.description: Dell and HPE this week both told investors they’ve become “different companies.” The two hardware giants made that assertion on their respective earnings calls this week. HPE went first, on Monday, when CEO Antonio Neri declared “We are now a fundamentally different company” after acquiring Juniper Networks and creating products “built to capitalize on the next phase of AI.” On Tuesday, Dell’s chief operating officer and vice chairman Jeff Clarke declared “We are now a different company” because the Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) has become the source of “the vast majority of our profit and growth.” HPE’s claim to having changed is perhaps more credible on the face of it, given that its acquisition of Juniper means it has become more of a networking player. Dell hasn’t made significant additions to its hardware portfolio, but there’s a big difference in its sources of revenue, which three years ago was just about evenly split between its infrastructure and client devices. In its Tuesday announcement, Dell revealed ISG revenue grew 198 percent year over year to $42 billion, while CSG racked up three percent growth to $12.9 billion – meaning Dell is now predominantly an infrastructure company. Clarke said he’s seen some companies deferring their PC purchases to buy AI hardware instead, and said Dell is re-assigning parts it ordered to build PCs and using them for servers instead. Dell exited its Q3 with a backlog of $32 billion worth of AI servers and is clearly aware that investors might worry that’s not a useful metric because some buyers’ dreams of operating neoclouds have struck financial or regulatory barriers. Clarke assured investors that Dell is “highly selective about the partners we work with” “Every AI order is vetted for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance, and access to land and power.” HPE also has wrinkles in its AI business, because buyers won’t stand for fat margins and that’s dented the company’s profits a little. Neri was able to point to AI-related revenue also rising sharply, up 68.6 percent year over year to $11.3 billion, while overall revenue climbed 50 percent to reach $14.5 billion. Networking grew at a more relaxed 12 percent. The CEO said HPE expects better growth ahead, because new server purchases create demand for networks and storage. He also pointed to HPE having the opportunity to sell its networking kit to other OEMs who build AMD’s Helios rack-scale systems. HPE predicted its next quarter will see revenue reach $14.0 billion to $14.6 billion, up 51 to 57 percent year over year. Dell is also optimistic that AI buyers will spend on kit beyond servers and GPUs and updated its full-year revenue outlook to $202 billion, $10 billion above its previous forecasts and up 78 percent year over year. ®

technology.title: AI godfather Yann LeCun torches Anthropic CEO over AI gatekeeping

It’s like the Ottoman Empire banning the printing press for Arabic so they would keep in control of the dogma.” LeCun is one of the most influential names in AI and ML. His team is credited with the development of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in the late ’80s during his time at Bell Labs. He later oversaw the development of Meta’s Llama herd of models as chief AI scientist before shifting gears away from LLMs to world model architectures like JEPA. He has also been a strong proponent of open source AI development and open models. Of the major model houses, Anthropic has taken the most hostile position against the adoption of open-weights models. Despite advocating against the unregulated diffusion of open models for years, Anthropic’s fearmonger-in-chief has maintained that the company isn’t opposed to them. “Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models,” Amodei wrote in a blog post earlier this year. technology.title: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
technology.description: Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis . The news follows several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by large language model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset. It's too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math. Tackling Riemann The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There's not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. This gives it significance for areas ranging from number theory to cryptography. technology.title: 'We are not ShinyHunters,' says criminal hacking crew that looks and acts just like ShinyHunters
technology.description: Inception, a new data theft and extortion gang that security researchers have theorized is a rebrand of the ShinyHunters group, “reject[s] this attribution” and claims it has no affiliation with any prior cybercrime enterprise. In a lengthy statement posted Tuesday and shared on X, the extortionists insist that they are a new group, with new operators, and that their alleged social engineering attacks aren’t copying anyone - but rather just abusing the weakest link in an organization’s security: “a human being holding a phone.” The rant follows a Monday report by Okta Threat Intelligence - along with social media speculation since Inception’s inception last week - that the newly emerged group is very likely ShinyHunters with a different name . Okta’s researchers based their analysis on the two groups’ shared infrastructure, plus Inception’s nearly identical tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA) requests. Inception apparently took offense to this. “We would like to address this once, clearly, and only once,” the crims' statement says. “We are not ShinyHunters. We were never ShinyHunters. We are Inception.” The gang argues that its overlapping domain registrars, hosting providers, and DNS services don’t prove anything. These are commodity services, “available to anyone who can pay for them,” Inception wrote. Plus, their similar methodologies don't necessarily make Inception a reboot. “That is not theft of tradecraft,” they wrote. “It is acknowledgment of a good idea – the same way every group after LockBit used a leak site, and nobody called them LockBit.” “Inception is a new group, with new operators, our own objectives, and our own name,” the statement continues. “What we share with the past is plumbing.” To be fair, the new crime crew has every reason to distance itself from ShinyHunters. That gang’s September FBI hack - plus several earlier digital heists during which the criminals stole information belonging to millions of people, including cancer patients , university and K-12 students - put a massive target on its collective backs. And while at least three ShinyHunters suspects were arrested in September and October, there's no confirmation that authorities have dismantled the entire operation. Plus, as a ShinyHunters spokesperson told The Register in an earlier interview, they and others in the crew started off as GnosticPlayers before rebranding as ShinyHunters in 2020 - so a reboot isn’t beyond the realm of possibility. Inception, for its part, says it “will not comment further on the ghost of ShinyHunters,” and it has its own work to do. And by work, it means copying ShinyHunters' playbook, stealing corporate data, and extorting victim companies for massive sums of money.®

science.title: SpaceX launches secretive spy satellites from California for US Space Force (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched another classified mission for the U.S. Space Force (USSF) today (Nov. 24), sending an unknown payload toward orbit from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Space Launch Complex-4E at TK11:08 a.m. ET (1508 GMT) , carrying the U.S. Space Force's USSF-266 mission. It was the fourth mission SpaceX has launched for the military branch this month. While details about the mission's payload weren't disclosed, it's the fifth space launch in support of U.S. national security in the last two weeks, and comes amid efforts by the Space Force to expand its communications and tracking capabilities. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two and a half minutes after liftoff, Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued toward low Earth orbit with the classified payload. The booster, meanwhile, began a descent toward SpaceX's Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific Ocean, where it touched down approximately eight and a half minutes after launch. Tuesday's launch marked the 29th flight for this Falcon 9 booster, B1081, which previously launched NASA 's Crew-7 astronaut mission to the International Space Station , the PACE and EarthCARE science satellites , two other classified Space Force launches (USSF-153 and USSF-481), and 16 Starlink missions. Previous classified Space Force launches have fueled speculation about the possible deployment of SpaceX's Starshield satellites, which are designed for national security applications. Starshield is an adapted spacecraft design developed from SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation that supports military operations with capabilities like Earth observation and secure communications. SpaceX has not confirmed whether USSF-266 is carrying Starshield spacecraft. USSF-266 follows three other classified Space Force missions launched by SpaceX from Vandenberg earlier this month: USSF-432 on Nov. 6, USSF-627 on Nov. 11 and USSF-317 on Nov. 20, as well as a National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) launch, NROL-136, on Nov. 22. Those missions were also launched aboard Falcon 9 rockets, also with undisclosed payloads.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 24, 1947: The US Navy launches the 1st Aerobee sounding rocket, but it didn't reach space
science.description: null On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere . After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets , the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched. Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space . (NASA and the U.S. military typically consider 50 miles the edge of space.) Mission control cut the flight short after about 30 seconds, because Aerobee started to yaw, and they wanted to keep it from going completely out of control. The first Aerobee sounding rocket launched on Nov. 24, 1947 under a project led by the U.S. Navy. (Image credit: U.S. Navy) Why it mattered Billed as the " most successful sounding rocket of the space age ," the initial Aerobee rocket was suborbital rocket designed to launch experment payload of up to 100 pounds (45 kilograms) to an altitude of 75 miles (121 kilometers) or so. "The Aerobee was designed to carry instruments aloft to collect data on the upper atmosphere and to place small animals in a weightless condition for physiological studies," the U.S. National Museum of the United States Air Force wrote in a mission overview . "It was launched by a solid-propellant booster engine of 18,000 pounds thrust that burned for only two and a half seconds." An Aerobee suborbital sounding rocket of the type designed to study Earth's atmosphere. (Image credit: NMMSH) While the first Aerobee rocket did not reach space , many more made successful launches in the decades that followed. Engineers made a steady stream of upgrades to the the Aerobee rocket, allowing to fly higher and launch heavier payloads into space. It was an Aerobee rocket that launched two Phillipine monkeys on a mission to study how the effects of rapid launch acceleration might affect their bodies, an experiment that was among the frst human physiology tests that paved the way for human spaceflight . More than 1,000 Aerobee rockets have launched since then, and the last one flew in January of 1985. Want more space history? science.title: Teams Lock in Mission Architecture for NASA’s SR-1 Freedom
science.description: 5 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) NASA’s Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit, cruises past Mars in this artist’s concept, demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion in deep space. Credit: NASA/Jonathan North NASA completed a major review for Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom and locked in key elements of the spacecraft, which is targeted to launch in 2028 and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion in deep space for the first time. Experts from across the agency, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), and industry met at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland for a major SR-1 mission design review in October. Several key decisions were made, propelling the mission from an early concept toward a defined spacecraft design. “SR-1 marks a pivotal step in how we travel through the solar system,” said Steve Sinacore, SR-1 Freedom program director. “This mission will be the first freight run on the railroad of the solar system, and the decisions we’re making now are laying the tracks for every nuclear-powered spacecraft that follows.” Planned for launch in late 2028, SR-1 will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall , a capsule carrying three next-generation helicopters, to Mars. Once deployed, the helicopters will study Martian geology and climate history, explore new terrain, and search for signs of subsurface ice. As NASA prepares for more ambitious exploration missions, future spacecraft and surface operations will require significantly more power than current systems can provide, particularly in environments where sunlight is limited or unavailable. SR-1 will demonstrate how fission power can enable long-duration missions, pave the way for reliable surface power systems to support NASA’s future Moon Base , and enable exploration deeper into the solar system. Key design decisions The SR-1 Freedom spacecraft design has evolved since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman first introduced the concept in March at the agency’s Ignition event, where leadership shared plans to develop a fission-powered spacecraft in time for the next Mars launch window. One significant change is to use a shorter boom than the one shown in early illustrations. The boom separates the reactor from the spacecraft’s main body, known as the Power and Propulsion Element. The shorter boom will reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design. Planned for launch in late 2028, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall to Mars. This infographic explains the components of the spacecraft. Credit: NASA/David Lam NASA and DOE experts also determined that improvements in shielding and spacecraft design will allow the reactor to operate closer to the rest of the spacecraft. This will simplify integration while maintaining the radiation protection needed for spacecraft electronics and the SkyFall payload.

science.title: 'Blade Runner 2099' executive producers talk architectural easter eggs and franchise continuity for Prime Video's new sci-fi series (interview)
science.description: null Prime Video's new " Blade Runner 2099 " series arrives Nov. 25, 2026, and it flips the cyberpunk universe on its head. The new show casts replicants as the dominant species on Earth, with humans relegated to second-class citizens after a global uprising. This dreary dystopian cyberpunk realm originates from sci-fi legend Phillip K. Dick's 1968 novel, "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?," and was then so vividly brought to life in Ridley Scott’s seminal 1982 adaptation, " Blade Runner ." The 2017 sequel, "Blade Runner 2049," was directed by "Arrival’s" and "Dune’s" Denis Villeneuve. Starring Michelle Yeoh, Hunter Schafer, Matthew Needham, Dimitri Abold, and Lewis Gribben, " Blade Runner 2099 " hails from creator and showrunner Silka Louisa and Alcon Entertainment founders Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, who executive produce with Ridley Scott's Scott Free Productions. Here, Yeoh's dying replicant blade runner Olwen unites with Schafer’s Cora, a human masquerading as a synthetic, to hunt down a dangerous rogue replicant that holds the key to a dark secret. (Image credit: Alberto Rodriguez/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images) We spoke to Kosove and Johnson about being respectful keepers of "Blade Runner's" creative flame, the pitch that sold them, and dipping back into Dick's original novel. "When the original film came out in 1982, and even when "2049" came out about a decade ago, a lot of things that these movies envisioned seemed far, far away and hard to comprehend," Kosovo tells Space. "The creation of artificial sentient beings. Today, sitting here in November of 2026, the world is catching up quicker to the world of 'Blade Runner,' with artificial technology and concerns of how do humans use this technology for our benefit without it taking over." "Silka came in several years ago and pitched her very simple idea, which was, the next chapter of 'Blade Runner' should be what happens when the replicants overtake their creators." explains Kosovo. "We thought that idea was going to be particularly resonant. It was simple to understand so new fans could enter the world without being steeped in the first two movies. And we thought it had logical continuity to the story canon that came before it. It checked a number of key boxes for us. Even though we talked to a number of showrunners who were much more established in their careers than Silka was at that point, she won the day with the most elegant idea in our opinion." science.title: 1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death
science.description: null As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper. New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed. NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas." Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf , the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived " red giant " phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris. During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space. To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming. "Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action." science.title: Double asteroid solar eclipse caught on camera | Space photo of the day for Nov. 24, 2026
science.description: null (Image credit: ESA) A spacecraft far from Earth beamed home a rare sight: a solar eclipse caused by one asteroid casting its shadow on another. What is it? The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system , which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos. In this image, Dimorphos' shadow can be seen on the surface of Didymos. The image was captured by the European Space Agency's (ESA's) Hera probe, which was sent to rendezvous with Didymos. Once there, Hera's job is to inspect the system to study the aftermath of NASA's historic DART mission (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), which slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in September 2022 in an attempt to alter its orbit and thus the trajectory of the entire two-asteroid system. Such missions, should they ever be needed in the future, could potentially redirect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. Why is it incredible? For one, this image is incredible given that it was beamed home by Hera while it approaches Didymos some 121 million miles (195 million kilometers) away from Earth. But more than that, this image reveals incredible details of the Didymos system. Scientists call Didymos a "rubble pile" asteroid , meaning it's a loose body made up of boulders, dust, gravel and other bits of the solar system held together by the asteroid's own gravity. In the image, many of these irregular boulders and rocks can be seen strewn across Didymos and its moonlet. Hera will reach the system on Nov. 25, and ESA will release the first full images from the mission.

science.title: China's Shenzhou-24 mission launches 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station
science.description: null China has launed an international astronaut to its Tiangong space station today (Nov. 24) for the first time ever, marking a significant milestone for international participation in the Chinese space program. A Long March 2F rocket lifted off with the Shenzhou-24 crew from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China today at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT and 8:18 a.m. Beijing time on Nov. 25). You can watch the liftoff live here at Space.com, courtesy of China Central Television (CCTV). China rolls out the Long March 2F rocket for its Shenzhou-24 astronaut mission on Nov. 17, 2026. (Image credit: CCTV) Shenzhou-24 is China's 18th crewed spaceflight to date and its 12th astronaut mission to Tiangong , a three-module station that the nation finished assembling in low Earth orbit in late 2022. Those numbers may sound rather prosaic. But today's flight makes history, marking the first time that China has ever launched a foreign national to space. That trailblazer is Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces who is the first person from his country ever to reach orbit. (Adventurer Namira Salim is the first Pakistani ever to fly to the final frontier, doing so on a Virgin Galactic suborbital mission in October 2023 .) China and Pakistan began paving Ali's path to Tiangong in February 2025 , with the signing of a spaceflight cooperation agreement in Islamabad. Pakistan then selected two astronaut candidates, who traveled to China for training. We didn't learn which Pakistani astronaut was picked for Shenzhou-24 until Monday night (Nov. 23), when China announced the mission's crew. This is not out of the ordinary, by the way; China generally doesn't reveal the identity of Shenzhou astronauts until the day before launch. This is in keeping with the nation's broader spaceflight ethos, which prizes keeping things close to the vest. Ali is flying as a payload specialist. The other Shenzhou-24 astronauts are commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi. Tang also flew on the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 missions, which launched in June 2021 and October 2023, respectively. He will be the first person to visit Tiangong three times, according to the state-run Xinhua news agency. Shenzhou-24 will be the first spaceflight for Wu. Tang and Wu are expected to live aboard Tiangong for six months, the usual Shenzhou rotation. But Ali will stay in orbit for just a week or so, coming back down to Earth with Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying of the Shenzhou-23 mission, which launched on May 24 . According to the South China Morning Post, the third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will stay behind when Ali leaves, living aboard Tiangong until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore become the first Chinese astronaut ever to spend a year in orbit, a milestone that will allow China to prep for long-duration missions to the moon and other deep-space locales.

science.title: Russia launches Progress 97 cargo ship to the International Space Station (video)
science.description: null Russia's latest freighter is on its way to the International Space Station. The robotic Progress 97 cargo craft launched atop a Soyuz rocket from the Russia-run Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan today (Nov. 24) at 5:17 a.m. EST (1013 GMT; 3:17 p.m. Baikonur time), carrying several tons of supplies for the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab. If all goes to plan, Progress 97 will arrive at the International Space Station (ISS) on Thursday (Nov. 26), docking with its Poisk module. But the freighter won't stay at that particular locale for long. A Russian Soyuz rocket launches the uncrewed Progress 97 cargo ship to the International Space Station from Baikonur Cosmodrome, Kazakhstan on Nov. 24, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) The cosmonauts currently living on the ISS — Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Sergey Teteryatnikov — will unload Progress 97 through Poisk. But the freighter will then hop over to a different port, according to journalist and space historian Anatoly Zak: the aft one of the PrK transfer tunnel, which leads to Russia's Zvezda service module. The PrK port is the best site for engine burns that boost the orbit of the ISS, a service that Progress freighters regularly provide. But Progress 97 cannot unload its cargo through that port because the PrK transfer tunnel has been sealed off, due to an ongoing air leak that was first documented in 2019. Progress-97 is therefore "the first cargo mission scheduled to unload its cargo and perform orbit corrections of the ISS at different docking ports," Zak wrote on the site he runs, RussianSpaceWeb.com. Progress 96 cargo spacecraft packed with science and supplies approaches the International Space Station for a docking on Sept. 19, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) The Progress 97 mission, which Russia calls Progress MS-36, was originally expected to launch this past August, according to Zak. But the liftoff was pushed back several times, most significantly by the collapse of the service platform at Baikonur's Site 31 in November 2025. It took Russia about three months to repair the platform, leading to a series of delays. Progress 97 will likely stay docked to the ISS for about six months, after which it will be loaded up with trash and sent home to burn up in Earth's atmosphere . Japan's HTV-X vehicle and Northrop Grumman's Cygnus spacecraft are similarly expendable. The only currently operational ISS cargo craft that's reusable is SpaceX's Dragon capsule, which makes parachute-aided ocean splashdowns at the end of its missions.

science.title: Severe eczema healed by novel immune-calming pill in clinical trial
science.description: Eczema causes itchy, inflamed rashes on the skin Evgeniia Gordeeva/Getty Images Over a third of people with moderate to severe eczema taking part in a clinical trial have seen their skin completely or almost completely clear up after taking an experimental pill for four months. The drug targets a part of the immune system that causes eczema when it gets stuck in overdrive, and it may be preferable to the current standard treatment, which has to be injected. “It definitely looks promising,” says Gayle Ross at the Royal Melbourne Hospital. Read more Chronic inflammation messes with your mind. Here’s how to calm it Eczema, or atopic dermatitis, is a chronic skin condition characterised by itchy, inflamed rashes and broken skin that can become infected. It is driven by an overactive immune pathway involving two signalling proteins called interleukin-4 and interleukin-13. Advertisement In 2017, the companies Sanofi and Regeneron received approval in the US for their jointly developed eczema drug dupilumab, which blocks interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 signalling. But, although the medication is effective , it has had limited uptake in the US because it must be injected under the skin and costs up to $59,000 per year for those without insurance coverage. Now, another company, Kymera Therapeutics, has developed an alternative treatment that can be taken in pill form, called KT-621. It targets the same immune pathway as dupilumab but degrades a protein called STAT6 that is activated downstream from interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 in the development of eczema. Free newsletter Sign up to Health Check Sign up to newsletter In the clinical trial , 244 adults with an average age of 39 and moderate to severe eczema were randomised to take KT-621 at three different doses or a placebo pill every day for 16 weeks. Those taking the most effective dose experienced an average 72 per cent reduction in their eczema severity on a standard scale, compared to 27 per cent in the placebo group. What’s more, 38 per cent of participants taking KT-621 had completely healed skin or almost completely healed skin by the end of the trial. “These results exceeded our expectations,” said Terence Rooney , the chief medical officer of Kymera Therapeutics, when announcing the results in a webcast on 23 November. He showed before-and-after photos of one man who had had severe eczema all over his torso at the beginning of the trial, which disappeared by the end. “It’s obviously early days and the trial had relatively small patient numbers, but [KT-621] looks like it has similar efficacy to dupilumab, which is currently the standard of care for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis, and it would be nice to have an oral option as opposed to an injection,” says Ross. science.title: Eruption Extends Iwo Jima’s Beach
science.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Eruption Extends Iwo Jima’s… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search October 26 November 11 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 26 November 11 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 26 November 11 Curtain Toggle 2-Up A volcanic eruption in the shallows near Iwo Jima has extended the Japanese island’s famed black sand beaches, at least temporarily. Signs of unrest began in late October 2026. On October 27, seismic sensors recorded a sharp uptick in activity, and Japan’s Meteorological Agency reported that the first photographs of the eruption were captured. Soon after, sensors on several satellites began to capture an array of observations. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured the left image on October 26, when the coast was still quiet. On November 11, Landsat 9 got its first clear view of the land the submarine volcano has built (right). A shortwave-infrared signature, a sign of the eruption’s heat, is shown in orange. A faint gray volcanic plume drifts southeast of the vent, and a streak of floating pumice stretches across the water in the same direction. A false-color backscatter radar image from the NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite offered an even earlier look at the eruption. On October 28, despite heavy cloud cover, the radar detected a large disturbance in the water in the same area that erupted in December 2023. When the clouds cleared in early November, the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors on NASA and NOAA satellites also captured signs of the ongoing eruption’s volcanic plumes and infrared signature . Japan’s Coast Guard released a report on November 16 confirming the formation of new land connected to the pre-existing beach. The eruption appears to have added roughly 50 hectares (125 acres) of new beach, about the area of 90 American football fields. That would enlarge the island by about 1.7 percent. The new land adjoins the southeast beach where American troops landed on February 19, 1945, beginning one of the bloodiest battles in the history of the U.S. Marines. The location of the eruption is no surprise to scientists. In addition to the 2023 eruption off the southeast coast, Iwo Jima had an eruption off its west coast in August 2025, said Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center. science.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust
science.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal. "We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," Aymeric Goyer, associate professor at OSU's Department of Botany and Plant Pathology, said in a statement . "That's an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the moon." To grow the spuds, the scientists used five different materials that are similar to regolith , the dust and rocks that cover the moon's surface. The moon contains various regions with unique surface makeups, so the materials they used simulated regolith from both lunar mare and lunar highland regions. The secret ingredient was vermicompost, a soil that's rich in nutrients. The team added different levels of vermicompost to the simulated regolith to grow the potatoes. They figured out that fake regolith mixed with 30 percent vermicompost worked about as well as growing potatoes with regular soil. Oregon State University researchers David Handy and Aymeric Goyer studying potatoes grown in lunar regolith. (Image credit: Aymeric Goyer/David Handy/OSU) "We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith by reducing plant exposure to harmful compounds," David Handy, a postdoctoral researcher in Goyer's lab, said in the same statement. The idea is that astronauts in the future could bring a little nutrient-rich soil with them and mix it with regolith to grow potatoes. After all, it'd cost a ton to ship all that food from Earth. NASA funding supported this research.

Tariq is the Editor-in-Chief of Space.com based out of our New York City office and joined the team in 2001, first as an intern and staff writer, and later as an editor. He covers human spaceflight, exploration and space science, as well as skywatching and entertainment. He became Space.com's Managing Editor in 2009 and Editor-in-Chief in 2019. Hailing from Stockton, California (where he attended the same high school as NASA astronaut Jose Hernandez), Tariq studied print journalism and astronomy at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, earning a bachelor's degree in journalism in 1999 along with a minor in astronomy. He then served as a staff reporter for The Los Angeles Times covering education and city beats in La Habra and Fullerton in Orange County for the Our Times sections.

In 2000, Tariq became the city reporter for the Huntington Beach Independent, a weekly publication of the Los Angeles Times, covering local politics and events, crime, business and environmental issues. He left the Los Angeles Times in 2001 to study science journalism at New York University, where he earned a master's degree in 2002 from NYU's Science and Environmental Reporting Program (now the Science, Health and Environmental Reporting Program) under the direction of space reporter William Burrows.

Tariq first joined Space.com as an intern in September 2001 while also serving as a research assistant for nutrition writer Gary Taubes and writing freelance projects, where his work appeared in The Scientist and Laboratory Equipment Magazine.
